service_list.name: Roof Replacements
service_list.brief: Remove ageing, damaged, tiled, corrugated, asbestos cement, or metal roofs and install new Colorbond or metal roofing with sarking, anticon, battens, flashings, clean handover, and a 10-year workmanship warranty.

service_list.name: New Roofs
service_list.brief: Design, estimate, schedule, and install Colorbond and metal roofs for new residential builds, extensions, unit developments, display homes, and builder-led projects.

service_list.name: Gutter & Pipe Replacement
service_list.brief: Supply and fit Colorbond gutters, fascia, downpipes, and leaf-guard options to improve drainage and reduce water damage risk.

service_list.name: Metal Roofing Replacement/Re-roofing
service_list.brief: Replace older roofing systems with modern metal roofing for homes and commercial sites, including tile-to-tin and tile-to-Colorbond conversions.

service_list.name: Architectural Claddings
service_list.brief: Provide associated metal cladding and architectural cladding services for residential and commercial projects.

service_list.name: Colorbond Claddings
service_list.brief: Install Colorbond cladding systems as part of metal roofing and external envelope projects.

service_list.name: Fascia Cover
service_list.brief: Install fascia covers and related roof edge metalwork as listed in external service directories.

service_list.name: Leaf Guard
service_list.brief: Install leaf-guard options alongside guttering to protect drainage systems.

service_list.name: Roof Repairs & Leak Detection
service_list.brief: Provide roof repair and leak detection services for homes and businesses across regional and metro service areas.

service_list.name: Tile to Tin Roof Restorations
service_list.brief: Convert tiled roofs to tin or Colorbond metal roofing, improving weather protection, weight, drainage, and street appeal.

service_list.name: Unit Developments
service_list.brief: Deliver metal roofing installations for multi-unit residential developments.

service_list.name: Commercial Projects
service_list.brief: Manage larger commercial roofing projects with estimating, scheduling, installation, and credit account support.

service_list.name: Asbestos Roof Removal and Replacement
service_list.brief: Remove asbestos cement roof sheeting and replace with Colorbond metal roofing, following Victorian regulations, containment, transport, disposal, and independent clearance certificate requirements.

testimonials.quote: Called Hayden to provide a quote on re roofing our house he returned our enquiry quickly and the quote was clearly detailed and explained. Given a start date and can say the communication was great the end result was amazing. Before and after photos show the difference. Thank you
testimonials.author: Wayne Watson

testimonials.quote: I was unable to get a roof replacement for 6 months in Hamilton. I saw Vic West add on Facebook so I gave them a call. Hayden promptly gave me quote and came straight away to measure up. Before I knew it 2 teams of trades were here and off with the old roof new battens and sisal new sheets on capped and flashed all in one day. Vic West are a professional team and I highly recommend.
testimonials.author: Roland Peacock

testimonials.quote: Replacing your roof is such an overwhelming thing but Hayden was amazing from first phone call to being on time with appointments, quotes (which was well below what we were expecting 😊) and getting the job done so quickly!! He and his team were wonderful making quick work of getting the old roof off and new one on and cleaning up as well and it looks unbelievable like a new house! I couldn’t recommend Vicwest Roofing enough!!!
testimonials.author: Rebecca Schultz

testimonials.quote: These guys did a top job for me, going from tile to tin in Wendouree. Would recommend them 100%. Done in two days. Great effort. Thanks again. Cheers Don
testimonials.author: Donald Stewart

testimonials.quote: Hayden and his team replaced a rusting old iron roof on my old Creswick cottage with Colorbond ( Pale Eucalypt). Parts of the house were over 100 years old and it wasn’t an easy job. There were solar panels to be removed and replaced as well. The team did a great job, arriving very early each day and working solidly until knock off time. They ran a very tidy worksite and obviously took pride in workmanship, which was good to see. All the debris was removed at the end.
testimonials.author: Helen Hanson

project_descriptions: Tile to Colorbond roof replacement, Alfredton VIC: removed ageing tiled roof, replaced weakened battens, installed sarking and anticon, then fitted a new Colorbond metal roof in Monument with custom flashings.

Heritage Roof Replacement with Custom Flashings, Creswick VIC: replaced ageing corrugated roofing on a period home, matched heritage profiles, installed custom-folded flashings to chimneys, valleys, and verandah.

Metal Roof Replacement, Wendouree VIC: removed failing corrugated metal roofing, replaced damaged battens, installed sarking and anticon, then fitted new Colorbond metal roofing with ridge cappings and flashings.

Asbestos Roof Removal and Replacement, Highton VIC: safely removed asbestos cement Super Six sheeting and installed Colorbond metal roofing with licensed removal, containment, transport, disposal, and clearance certificate.

Tile to Colorbond Roof Replacement, Williamstown VIC: replaced ageing concrete tiles with Colorbond roofing built for coastal conditions around Melbourne’s west.
Old Creswick cottage roof: replaced rusting old iron roof with Pale Eucalypt Colorbond on a house partly over 100 years old, including solar panel removal and replacement coordination.

narrative.executive_summary: Vicwest Roofing is a Ballarat-region metal roofing and roof replacement business trading under VICWEST GROUP PTY LTD, ABN 69 622 718 361. The Google Business Profile lists the business at Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe VIC 3356, with weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and a primary mobile contact of 0403 554 592. The owned website positions the company as “Roof Replacement Experts” serving Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Castlemaine, Creswick, Maryborough, and towns within 100km of Ballarat. The service offer is strongly centred on roof replacements, new Colorbond and metal roofs, gutters, fascia, downpipes, leaf guard, and larger residential or commercial roofing work. The most credible differentiator is the combination of scale and speed: customers repeatedly mention Hayden, fast quoting, two teams of trades, same-day or two-day replacement outcomes, tidy worksites, and workmanship that transforms old roofs into “like a new house” results. The website backs this with a 10-year workmanship warranty, over 20 years’ experience, licensed installers, CAD estimating, pre and post inspections, and multiple named case studies in Alfredton, Creswick, Wendouree, Highton, Bendigo, and Williamstown. The redesign should not invent a new brand; it should sharpen the current no-nonsense, trade-credible identity and put the strongest proof above the fold: 20+ years, 10-year warranty, Ballarat base, service within 100km, real project photos, and a visible call/quote path.
narrative.company_background: The legal entity behind Vicwest Roofing is VICWEST GROUP PTY LTD, an Australian Private Company with ABN 69 622 718 361 and ACN 622 718 361. The ABN has been active since 9 November 2017, with GST registration effective from the same date and trading name VICWEST ROOFING. External directory data from Localsearch states the business has been “Trading for 9 years,” which broadly aligns with the 2017 ABN start date by 2026. The public website also claims “over 20 years’ experience,” which should be treated as team or founder experience rather than legal entity age unless the client confirms the exact backstory. WHOIS data is privacy-redacted and does not provide a domain registration date; Wayback has a last snapshot dated 20 April 2025 but no first snapshot date in the provided data, so domain age cannot be stated. The business has evolved from a local Ballarat roofing operator into a larger Western Victoria roofing company with substantial builder-facing capability. The About page describes Vicwest as “one of Western Victoria’s largest and most dedicated roofing companies,” with “large-scale, professional services” and a focus on long-lasting client relationships. The services and careers pages show a company with structured estimating, scheduling, credit accounts, apprentices, qualified roof plumbers, subcontractors, and commercial client processes. The credit application page is especially important: it signals repeat builder or trade relationships, asks for ABN, director/proprietor details, and three trade credit references, and says credit is for business purposes only. Customer reviews put a human face on the company through Hayden, who is repeatedly named as the person who quotes, measures, communicates, and coordinates the work. This gives the redesign two truths to balance: Vicwest is large enough for two teams and commercial credit accounts, but still local and personal enough that homeowners remember Hayden arriving, measuring, explaining, and making the job feel manageable.
narrative.team_and_culture: The strongest team signal is practical, not corporate. Reviews and social mentions describe a working culture built around speed, tidy execution, and crew coordination. Roland Peacock’s Hamilton review says that after Hayden quoted and measured, “2 teams of trades were here” and completed removal of the old roof, new battens, sisal, new sheets, caps, and flashings “all in one day.” An Instagram mention says “two large, efficient teams” help Vicwest projects run “on time and on budget, with no delays.” Helen Hanson’s Creswick review describes the crew arriving “very early each day and working solidly until knock off time,” running “a very tidy worksite,” and taking obvious pride in workmanship. Rebecca Schultz says Hayden and his team made “quick work of getting the old roof off and new one on and cleaning up as well.” The careers pages reinforce the same culture from inside the business: Vicwest says employees are “the backbone of our success,” and recruits roofing tradesmen, apprentices, qualified roof plumbers, and subcontractors specialising in fascia, guttering, and metal roofing. The tone is trade-professional and growth-oriented: supportive environment, ongoing training, collaboration, precise installations, and workmanship that “stands the test of time.” The redesign should show the team as capable crews, not anonymous stock-photo tradies. A “Meet Hayden and the Vicwest team” section can acknowledge the personal contact customers value while also presenting the broader operation: estimators trained in CAD, planners who coordinate with builders, licensed installers, apprentices learning the full job from start to finish, and qualified roof plumbers handling residential and large-scale commercial work. The one negative review complains about phone responsiveness and disorganisation, so the new site should use clearer response expectations, quote forms, plan upload, and visible office hours to reduce that risk.
narrative.service_scope_detailed: Roof replacements are the core offer. The homepage calls Vicwest a local specialist for roof replacements in Ballarat and surrounding towns within 100km, and the dedicated roof replacement page adds Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Creswick, Ararat, Stawell, Castlemaine, and Melbourne’s western suburbs. The process is repeatedly described: remove the old roof, replace weakened or damaged battens, install sarking and anticon, fit a new Colorbond or metal roof, complete custom flashings to penetrations, valleys, chimneys, and verandahs, then hand over a clean site with a 10-year workmanship warranty. The pain point is ageing, leaking, rusting, weathered, or storm-damaged roofing that makes homeowners anxious. Rebecca’s review captures the emotional state: “Replacing your roof is such an overwhelming thing.” The ideal output is a tighter, lighter, weather-resistant roof with better drainage and street appeal. Named examples include Alfredton tile-to-Colorbond in Monument, Wendouree corrugated metal replacement, Bendigo tile-to-Colorbond, and Williamstown tile-to-Colorbond built for coastal conditions. New roofs are the builder-facing and new-home side of the business. The New Roofs page targets people “Building your dream home” and says Vicwest works closely with builders and homeowners to deliver precision, durability, and aesthetics for Australian designs and conditions. The page adds operational proof: estimators are trained in the latest CAD software, provide fast residential estimates, and aim to provide the right product for the right price. Scheduling and installation are positioned as a differentiator, with communication with builders used to follow build progress and integrate jobs seamlessly into schedule. Pre and post inspections are conducted for safety, efficiency, and standards. Gutter, fascia, downpipe, and leaf-guard replacement supports the roof envelope. The homepage describes leak-free gutter replacement around Ballarat, with Colorbond gutters, fascia, downpipes, and leaf-guard options to improve drainage and protect property from water damage. This service should be positioned as both a standalone drainage fix and a smart add-on during full roof replacement. Metal cladding, architectural cladding, Colorbond cladding, fascia cover, unit developments, and commercial projects come from Localsearch and social mentions. These broaden the offer beyond simple residential replacement and should sit under a “Builders & Commercial” or “Metal Roofing Systems” page. Asbestos roof removal and replacement is explicitly described in the Highton case study: asbestos cement “Super Six” sheeting was removed and replaced with Colorbond metal roofing, with Victorian regulations, licensed removal, containment, transport, disposal, and independent clearance certificate. This page requires careful compliance wording and confirmation from Vicwest about whether removal is in-house or subcontracted. Roof repairs and leak detection appear in Localsearch and the roof replacement page mentions roof repairs for homes and businesses, but the owned site gives less process detail. Treat repair as a secondary service unless the client confirms it is a major revenue line.
narrative.service_area: Vicwest Roofing should be presented as Ballarat-based with a broad Western Victoria and regional reach, not merely a single-suburb roofer. The Google Business Profile places the business at Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe VIC 3356, and the contact page lists 3/31 Icon Drive, Delacombe, Victoria, as well as Ballarat wording. The homepage says Vicwest serves Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Castlemaine, Creswick, Maryborough, and all towns within 100km of Ballarat. The About page expands this into “Based in Ballarat and Geelong,” with coverage across Geelong, the Bellarine Peninsula, the Surf Coast, Ballarat, surrounding regions, and “all areas in between.” The roof replacement page adds Ararat, Stawell, and Melbourne’s western suburbs, while project pages and reviews add Hamilton, Wendouree, Alfredton, Highton, Bendigo, Williamstown, Yarraville, Seddon, Altona, Kangaroo Flat, Golden Square, Strathdale, and Epsom. Project image filenames add Gordon, Lucas, Scarsdale, Display Homes, and Ingenia Homes, which can support gallery filtering but should not be overclaimed as service-area pages unless copy is written carefully. The redesign should build a service-area hub around Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, and Melbourne’s west, then use project-led location pages for Alfredton, Creswick, Wendouree, Highton, Bendigo, and Williamstown. The copy should avoid suggesting emergency coverage everywhere; instead, state that larger roof replacements, builder projects, and metal roofing work are assessed across Western Victoria and selected Melbourne western suburbs.
narrative.customer_voice: The customer voice is unusually useful because it names the emotional friction around roof replacement and the proof points that matter. Customers talk about anxiety, response time, price surprise, speed, cleanup, and the visual transformation after the job. Rebecca Schultz opens with the phrase the website should use: “Replacing your roof is such an overwhelming thing.” She then resolves that concern through Hayden’s behaviour: “amazing from first phone call,” on time with appointments, quote “well below what we were expecting,” and fast completion. Roland Peacock’s review is a logistics proof story: after being unable to get a roof replacement for six months in Hamilton, he called Vicwest from a Facebook ad, Hayden promptly quoted and measured, then “2 teams of trades” completed the old roof removal, battens, sisal, new sheets, caps, and flashings “all in one day.” Donald Stewart gives a simple local conversion proof point: “going from tile to tin in Wendouree,” “Done in two days,” and “Would recommend them 100%.” Helen Hanson’s review provides heritage, complexity, and workmanship language: an old Creswick cottage, parts over 100 years old, solar panels removed and replaced, early starts, tidy worksite, pride in workmanship, all debris removed, and even help finding an aerial installer to avoid new roof penetrations. Wayne Watson adds quote clarity and communication: Hayden returned the enquiry quickly, the quote was “clearly detailed and explained,” the start date was given, and “the end result was amazing.” These should shape the redesign’s copy. Instead of generic “quality roofing,” use phrases like “clearly detailed quote,” “old roof off, new roof on,” “tidy site handover,” “tile to tin,” “built for Victorian weather,” “before and after photos,” and “looks like a new house.” The negative review about poor phone answering should not be ignored; the website should provide multiple reliable contact routes and expectation-setting to protect trust.
narrative.brand_voice_and_visual: The current brand reads industrial, straightforward, and trade-credible. The extracted brand colours are near-black #0F1115, grey #6D6E71, muted gold #C5A572, white #FFFFFF, and soft grey #F4F4F5. This palette suits metal roofing because it feels structural and practical without becoming overly dark. The wordmark imagery and suggested heading style lean geometric and condensed; Inter Tight for headings and Inter for body would support a clean, modern build while preserving the existing identity. The website’s current phrases are useful but need hierarchy: “Roof Replacement Experts,” “The Leaders in Metal Roofing Solutions,” “Real Projects, Real Results,” and “on time, on budget, and built to last.” The voice should be confident but not polished into corporate emptiness. Sample brand paragraph for homeowners: “Replacing a roof is a big decision. Vicwest Roofing gives you a clearly detailed quote, practical advice on Colorbond and metal roofing options, and a crew that works cleanly from old roof removal through to final handover.” Sample builder paragraph: “For builders, timing matters. Our estimating team works from plans, our scheduling team stays close to build progress, and our installers complete each roof to a high standard with pre and post inspections.” Sample regional paragraph: “Based in Delacombe and working across Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, and Western Victoria, Vicwest handles roof replacements for homes, commercial sites, and larger residential developments.” Sample proof paragraph: “Customers describe same-day and two-day roof replacements, tidy worksites, early starts, clear communication, and roofs that make an old house look new again.” Visually, the site should lead with real roof photography, before/after project pairs, Colorbond colour references like Monument and Pale Eucalypt where verified, and practical proof chips rather than decorative trade clichés.
narrative.competitive_positioning: Vicwest’s strongest competitive position is the combination of local Ballarat credibility, broader Western Victoria reach, metal-roof specialisation, and team capacity. Many roofers can claim quality workmanship; fewer have the evidence to talk about two large teams, CAD-trained estimators, commercial credit accounts, builder scheduling, named case studies, and customer stories where entire replacements happen in one or two days. The redesign should position Vicwest as the practical choice for homeowners who want a major roof replacement handled without drama and for builders who need reliable metal roofing scheduling across Ballarat and regional Victoria. The point of difference is not luxury; it is dependable throughput, clean process, and proven project work. Real proof includes a 10-year workmanship warranty, over 20 years’ experience, ABN-active company status since 2017, Google rating 4.1 from 18 reviews, and testimonials mentioning Hayden, fast quotes, clear explanations, early starts, cleanup, and tidy handover. AI-inferred positioning: the main competitor set is likely local solo roof plumbers, general roof repair operators, and larger building envelope contractors. Vicwest can sit between those categories: personal enough for a Creswick cottage or Wendouree tile-to-tin job, but scaled enough for display homes, Ingenia Homes, unit developments, and commercial projects. The website should not overemphasise emergency leak repairs if replacement and new builds are the stronger revenue lines. It should instead own “metal roof replacement and new roofing across Western Victoria,” supported by project-led SEO pages.
narrative.trust_signals_catalog: Trust signals should be made explicit and repeated in high-conversion areas. Legal and operating proof: VICWEST GROUP PTY LTD, ABN 69 622 718 361, Australian Private Company, active since 9 November 2017, GST registered, trading name VICWEST ROOFING. Location proof: Google Business Profile address at Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe VIC 3356, plus contact-page address at 3/31 Icon Drive, Delacombe/Ballarat. Experience proof: the owned website claims “over 20 years’ experience,” while Localsearch states “Trading for 9 years,” so use the wording “20+ years’ roofing experience” and separately “ABN active since 2017” unless the client confirms founding history. Warranty proof: homepage and roof replacement pages state roof replacements are backed by a 10-year workmanship warranty, and the New Roofs page says all work is backed by a comprehensive warranty. Review proof: GBP rating 4.1 from 18 reviews, with strong five-star quotes from Wayne, Roland, Rebecca, Donald, Brad, and Helen. Project proof: named project pages in Alfredton, Creswick, Wendouree, Highton, Bendigo, and Williamstown, plus large image galleries for Scarsdale, Gordon, Lucas, Display Homes, and Ingenia Homes. Missing trust proof: VBA licence, insurance certificate, and verified team headcount.
narrative.visitor_personas: The homeowner persona is often anxious, practical, and comparing options after noticing an old, rusting, tiled, leaking, or storm-damaged roof. Rebecca’s line “Replacing your roof is such an overwhelming thing” should guide this journey. They need to know whether Vicwest services their suburb, whether Colorbond is suitable, what happens to old tiles or iron, how long the job will take, how the site is cleaned, and whether the quote will be clear. Hero, roof replacement, before/after projects, warranty, reviews, and quote CTA should serve this visitor. The builder persona cares less about reassurance and more about estimating, scheduling, accuracy, and no delays. The New Roofs page says estimators use CAD software and the team coordinates with builder progress, with pre and post inspections. The Instagram mention says plans can be sent to estimating@vicwestroofing.com.au. This persona needs plan upload, credit application, service capacity, and contact details for estimating. The commercial general contractor or developer persona is looking for evidence of scale: commercial projects, unit developments, metal claddings, fascia, guttering, Colorbond systems, and credit accounts. The site should show a commercial capability page and a simple path to apply for credit or send tender documents. The insurance or storm-damage visitor is ai-inferred from the website’s mention of storm damage and roof repairs. They need inspection, documentation, quote clarity, and help understanding whether repair or replacement is appropriate. The heritage homeowner persona is grounded in Helen Hanson’s Creswick cottage review and the Creswick heritage case study: they care about matching profiles, custom flashings, chimneys, verandahs, solar panels, aerials, and preserving character while improving weatherproofing.
narrative.pricing_and_sales_cycle: No fixed prices or rate card appear in the supplied corpus, so the website should not quote dollar amounts. However, there are useful pricing signals. Rebecca Schultz says the quote was “well below what we were expecting,” which supports a “clear, practical quoting” message rather than a cheap-price promise. Wayne Watson says the quote was “clearly detailed and explained,” and that he was given a start date; this is important because roofing sales cycles are won on confidence, not just price. Roland Peacock’s review shows speed can be a major buying trigger: he had been unable to get a roof replacement for six months in Hamilton, called after seeing a Facebook ad, and Vicwest promptly measured and completed the job quickly. The sales cycle likely splits into homeowner and builder flows. Homeowners need phone response, site measure, written quote, timing estimate, material/colour decision, safety/access planning, roof removal, installation, cleanup, and warranty handover. Builders need plan-based estimating, CAD takeoff, scheduling around build progress, pre-start inspection, installation, post inspection, and account/credit handling. The redesign should offer two lead paths: “Get a Roof Replacement Quote” for homeowners and “Send Plans for Estimating” for builders. Quote forms should ask for property address/suburb, roof type, issue or project type, approximate timing, photos, plan upload where relevant, and whether solar panels, asbestos, chimneys, or access constraints are present. Phone remains essential for urgent and high-intent leads.
narrative.website_strategy: The recommended website should be a multi-page conversion and SEO asset built around proof, service clarity, and project evidence. The homepage should immediately state the core offer: metal roof replacement and new roofs across Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, and Western Victoria, with 20+ years’ experience, 10-year workmanship warranty, 4.1 Google rating from 18 reviews, and clear CTAs to call or request a quote. The Roof Replacements page should be the primary SEO and sales page, covering tile-to-Colorbond, corrugated metal replacement, asbestos replacement, heritage roofs, sarking, anticon, battens, flashings, cleanup, and warranty. The New Roofs page should target builders and homeowners building new homes, with CAD estimating, plan upload, scheduling, pre/post inspections, and credit account links. A Gutters, Fascia & Downpipes page should present drainage and leaf-guard services as add-ons and standalone work. A Builders & Commercial page should combine unit developments, commercial projects, architectural claddings, Colorbond claddings, fascia cover, credit accounts, and estimating@vicwestroofing.com.au. Projects should become a structured gallery with filters by location and service: Alfredton, Creswick, Wendouree, Highton, Bendigo, Williamstown, Scarsdale, Gordon, Lucas, Display Homes, and Ingenia Homes. The About page should explain ABN-active company history, Hayden, team culture, two teams, apprenticeship pathways, and Western Victoria reach. Service-area pages should exist for Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, and Melbourne’s West, with project proof embedded. Contact should include tap-to-call, quote form, plan upload, email, address by appointment only, hours, and map. Careers can remain but should be simplified into tradesmen, apprentices, qualified roof plumbers, and subcontractors.
narrative.header_components: The header should fix the current conversion gap identified in the audit: visitors do not see an obvious phone call action above the fold. Desktop header should include the Vicwest Roofing logo at left, navigation items Home, Roof Replacements, New Roofs, Projects, About, Service Areas, Careers, and Contact, plus a visible phone link “0403 554 592” and a primary “Get a Quote” button. For builder-heavy pages, the primary CTA can switch to “Send Plans.” The header should use the existing black/charcoal brand base with restrained gold accent for the CTA or active state. Mobile header should show logo, a phone icon or “Call” action, and menu icon. A sticky bottom mobile action bar should include “Call” and “Get Quote,” because mobile contact is currently hidden behind the menu. The menu should group services clearly rather than forcing every page into a long list. The header can include a thin trust strip beneath or inside the hero: “20+ years’ roofing experience,” “10-year workmanship warranty,” “Ballarat based,” and “Colorbond metal roofing.” The header should not bury the quote path behind Contact only.
narrative.footer_components: The footer should be treated as a trust and routing section, not a dumping ground. Include the logo, a short positioning line such as “Metal roof replacement, new roofs, guttering, fascia, downpipes, and Colorbond roofing across Ballarat and Western Victoria.” Contact details should list phone 0403 554 592, info@vicwestroofing.com.au, estimating@vicwestroofing.com.au for plans, and Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe VIC 3356, noting “by appointment only” because the contact page says this. Hours should be shown exactly from GBP: Monday to Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM, Saturday and Sunday closed. Business credentials should include “VICWEST GROUP PTY LTD trading as VICWEST ROOFING, ABN 69 622 718 361, GST registered.” If licence and insurance are supplied later, place them in the same line or a dedicated “Licences & Insurance” item. Footer navigation should include Roof Replacements, New Roofs, Gutters & Downpipes, Builders & Commercial, Projects, About, Careers, Credit Info, Contact, and main service-area pages. Add social links already found externally: Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube, but verify the exact official profiles before launch. Include a Google Maps link for Delacombe/Ballarat. Add small-print warranty wording that does not overpromise: “10-year workmanship warranty on eligible roof replacements; confirm warranty details in your quote.” The footer should also support SEO with a concise service-area list: Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Castlemaine, Creswick, Maryborough, Ararat, Stawell, and Melbourne’s western suburbs.
narrative.cta_strategy: The primary CTA should be “Get a Roof Replacement Quote” for homeowner pages and “Send Plans for Estimating” for builder/new-roof pages. The secondary CTA should be “Call 0403 554 592.” These should appear in the header, hero, after service sections, beside project case studies, below testimonials, and in the footer. Mobile should include sticky call and quote actions because the audit found contact is hidden behind the menu. The quote form should be short but useful: name, phone, email, property address or suburb, service needed, roof type if known, timing, message, photo upload, and checkbox options for solar panels, asbestos/suspected asbestos, chimneys, leaks, storm damage, new build plans, or commercial work. Builder forms should include company, ABN optional, project address, plans upload, preferred start timeframe, roofing/cladding scope, and whether they need a credit account. CTA copy should use real customer language: “Get a clearly detailed roof quote,” “Book a measure,” “Send plans for a fast estimate,” “Upgrade to Colorbond,” and “Ask about a 10-year workmanship warranty.” Avoid emergency claims unless the client confirms emergency availability. Use proof near every CTA: Roland’s “all in one day” quote, Rebecca’s “well below what we were expecting,” Wayne’s “clearly detailed and explained,” and Helen’s “tidy worksite.” For the negative phone responsiveness outlier, the site should show expected response times, weekday hours, and multiple channels so leads are not forced into one phone call attempt.

narrative.about_us_draft: Vicwest Roofing is a Ballarat-based metal roofing company servicing homeowners, builders, and commercial clients across Western Victoria. Trading as VICWEST ROOFING under VICWEST GROUP PTY LTD, the business operates from Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe and works across Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Castlemaine, Creswick, Maryborough, and surrounding towns. The company’s work is built around roof replacements, new Colorbond and metal roofs, guttering, fascia, downpipes, architectural claddings, unit developments, and larger commercial roofing projects. The public website describes Vicwest as one of Western Victoria’s largest and most dedicated roofing companies, with over 20 years’ roofing experience and a commitment to high-10-year workmanship warranty in writing, responsiveness, and long-term client relationships. For homeowners, that means a practical process from first call through to quote, measure, old roof removal, new roof installation, cleanup, and warranty handover. For builders, it means CAD-trained estimating, scheduling that stays close to build progress, pre and post inspections, and the ability to send plans directly for estimating. Customers often mention Hayden by name. They describe clear quotes, prompt measuring, being on time for appointments, early starts, tidy worksites, and crews who work solidly until the job is complete. One Hamilton customer said two teams arrived and completed the old roof removal, battens, sisal, sheets, caps, and flashings in one day. A Wendouree customer described a tile-to-tin conversion finished in two days. A Creswick customer praised the team for replacing a rusting old iron roof on a cottage partly over 100 years old, managing solar panels, removing debris, and preserving the home’s character. Vicwest’s aim is straightforward: deliver metal roofing work that is well planned, well communicated, and built to withstand Victorian weather.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: What areas does Vicwest Roofing service?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Vicwest Roofing is based at Shed 3/31 Icon Dr, Delacombe VIC 3356, and services Ballarat plus a broad Western Victoria area. The website names Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, Bacchus Marsh, Daylesford, Castlemaine, Creswick, Maryborough, Ararat, Stawell, the Bellarine Peninsula, Surf Coast, and Melbourne’s western suburbs. Project and review evidence also mentions Alfredton, Wendouree, Highton, Williamstown, Hamilton, Gordon, Lucas, Scarsdale, Kangaroo Flat, Golden Square, Strathdale, and Epsom.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: Do you replace tile roofs with Colorbond metal roofing?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Yes. The roof replacement page includes tile-to-Colorbond projects in Alfredton, Bendigo, and Williamstown, and a Google review mentions a tile-to-tin roof conversion in Wendouree completed in two days. The usual process described in the source material is removing ageing concrete tiles, replacing weakened battens, installing sarking and anticon, fitting new Colorbond metal roofing, and finishing with custom flashings and ridge cappings.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Timing depends on roof size, access, weather, safety requirements, roof condition, asbestos risk, solar panels, and material availability. Real reviews show Vicwest can move quickly on suitable jobs: Roland Peacock described two teams completing an old roof removal, battens, sisal, new sheets, caps, and flashings in one day, while Donald Stewart said his tile-to-tin job in Wendouree was done in two days. The quote process should confirm timing for each property.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: What warranty does Vicwest Roofing provide?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: The homepage and roof replacement page state that roof replacements are backed by a 10-year workmanship warranty. The New Roofs page also says all work is backed by a comprehensive warranty and that the support team can assist with questions or maintenance needs. The website should present this as a workmanship warranty and ask customers to confirm exact warranty terms in their written quote.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: Can builders send plans for estimating?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Yes. The New Roofs page says Vicwest estimators are trained in the latest CAD software and provide fast residential estimates. An Instagram mention specifically says builders can forward plans to estimating@vicwestroofing.com.au. For the new website, the builder CTA should be “Send Plans for Estimating,” with upload fields for plans, project address, timing, roofing or cladding scope, and company details.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: Does Vicwest Roofing work on new homes?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Yes. The New Roofs page is written for new residential builds and says Vicwest works closely with builders and homeowners to deliver roofing solutions focused on precision, durability, and aesthetics. It also says scheduling and installation are a differentiator because communication with the builder helps Vicwest follow build progress and integrate jobs efficiently into schedule.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: Do you handle gutters, fascia and downpipes?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Yes. The homepage lists gutter and pipe replacement, including Colorbond gutters, fascia, downpipes, and leaf-guard options. Localsearch also lists guttering, fascia cover, and leaf guard among the services. This should be positioned as both a standalone drainage service and a smart add-on during a roof replacement, especially where water damage, overflow, rust, or ageing roof edges are an issue.

The Highton case study states Vicwest safely removed asbestos cement roof sheeting and installed a new Colorbond metal roof, including sarking, anticon, and custom flashings. It says the work followed Victorian regulations, with licensed removal, containment, transport, disposal, and an independent clearance certificate. Before launch, Vicwest should confirm whether removal is performed directly or through licensed asbestos subcontractors.

Hayden is the named Vicwest contact in multiple customer reviews. Customers say Hayden returned enquiries quickly, provided detailed quotes, came to measure up, arrived on time for appointments, coordinated the team, and even helped a customer find an aerial installer to avoid putting new holes in a roof. His exact title should be confirmed before publication, but he is clearly a key customer-facing figure.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: What makes Vicwest different from other roofers?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: The strongest proof points are scale, speed, and process. The website describes Vicwest as one of Western Victoria’s largest roofing companies, while reviews and social mentions refer to two efficient teams, fast quoting, clean worksites, early starts, and on-time/on-budget delivery. The business also has CAD-trained estimators, builder scheduling processes, commercial credit account support, and named project examples across Ballarat, Geelong, Bendigo, and Melbourne’s west.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: Can Vicwest work on older or heritage-style homes?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Yes, based on the supplied project and review evidence. The Creswick heritage case study describes replacing an ageing corrugated roof on a period home, matching heritage profiles and installing custom-folded flashings to chimneys, valleys, and a verandah. Helen Hanson’s Creswick review also describes a cottage partly over 100 years old, with solar panels removed and replaced and debris removed at the end.

faq_topics_with_answers.q: How do I get a quote?
faq_topics_with_answers.a: Call 0403 554 592 during listed weekday hours, email info@vicwestroofing.com.au, or use the website quote form. Builders and project managers should send plans to estimating@vicwestroofing.com.au. The ideal quote request should include property address or suburb, photos, current roof type, preferred timing, known issues such as leaks or rust, and whether there are solar panels, chimneys, asbestos concerns, or access constraints.
